breaking.headline: Trump calls pre-election GDP figures 'fake,' demands Commerce probe
breaking.fact: Trump demanded an immediate investigation Thursday, calling the Bureau of Economic Analysis revision of third-quarter GDP to 4.3% — up from the 3.4% advance estimate — a 'massive, and purposeful, error' tied to the Nov. 3 midterms; the BEA says revisions reflect more complete data, with the final estimate due Dec. 23.

breaking.headline: Judge blocks FCC's early review of ABC station licenses
breaking.fact: Judge Loren AliKhan granted Disney a preliminary injunction Wednesday, finding the FCC's early review of eight ABC-owned stations was likely retaliation for programming critical of Trump and a First Amendment violation; the FCC called the ruling wrong and said it expects to prevail.

breaking.headline: FedEx jet overruns Miami runway, snarling Thanksgiving eve travel
breaking.fact: FedEx Flight 910, an MD-11 freighter from Memphis, overran Runway 26R at Miami International about 8:40 PM Wednesday in heavy rain; both crew members were unhurt, but the FAA ground stop left the airport at reduced capacity and delays topped three and a half hours into Thursday.

breaking.headline: Thanksgiving storms flood both coasts; New Jersey under emergency
breaking.fact: All of New Jersey is under a state of emergency and parts of New York are too, with gusts topping 50 mph along the I-95 corridor, while record king tides flooded the California coast and tore down part of Pacifica's pier; heavy snow buried parts of Missouri and Illinois, with 14 inches at Ste. Genevieve.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide kept climbing through the U.S. holiday, closing Thursday in Paris at €190.32, up 1.0%, as the CAC 40 jumped 1.8%. At the ECB's Nov 26 reference rate of 1.0975 the quote converts to $208.88, not far from the year's high of €194.70. Steady European industrial-gas demand is doing the work here, and with Wall Street dark until Friday, the Paris close is the freshest print on the board.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic ended Wednesday at $82.79, up 1.1%, holding just under its $83 IPO price as the AI selloff paused for the holiday. The math world is still waiting on its Nov 20 Navier-Stokes blow-up claim with NYU's Tristan Buckmaster, whose numerical certificate has yet to be released, so the proof stays unverified. U.S. markets are closed for Thanksgiving; the next read comes in Friday's thin half session.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: The Treasury-bill fund ticked up a penny Wednesday to $91.64, doing what it is built for while the Nasdaq plunged 4.6% intraday and the VIX spiked to 28.29. Its distribution yield is 4.04%, on a $0.30849-per-share payout made Nov 5. In a week when growth stocks whipsawed, BIL's quiet steadiness is the point — and with a December hike priced near 95%, its yield should stay pinned to the front of the curve.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet gave back 2.1% Wednesday to close at $273.10, caught in the chip-led selloff as the Nasdaq slid 0.6% and hot PCE data pushed December hike odds toward 95%. There was no Alphabet-specific news behind the drop — it was the rate-sensitive growth trade unwinding. S&P futures are up 0.7% into Friday's half session, but the stock needs tech sentiment to stop sliding before it can find a floor.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly eased 1.1% Wednesday to $1,392.22, giving back part of Tuesday's 3.2% jump as money rotated into defensive names and out of growth. The pullback was modest next to the Nasdaq's 4.6% intraday plunge, and Lilly held up well through the afternoon recovery. With markets closed for Thanksgiving, the drugmaker's next move waits on Friday's thin half session and whether the safety trade holds.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere rose 2.0% Wednesday to $301.99 while the broader market fell apart intraday, and the energy backdrop only strengthened Thursday. Brent settled at $96.57 after Houthi strikes on Saudi ports and Iranian mines hit tankers in the strait, with WTI at $84.84. Tight global gas markets and rising Gulf tensions keep favoring U.S. LNG exporters, and Cheniere's run looks more durable than a one-day bounce.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia dropped 3.9% Wednesday to $149.30, giving back more of Monday's 31% surge after Huang returned, and S&P put its AA rating on CreditWatch Negative on governance grounds. Thursday added overhang: the FT reported Nvidia halted server shipments to four Southeast Asian nations under new U.S. export rules, pending Washington guidance on future sales. Friday's thin session tests whether it steadies.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer finished flat Wednesday at $28.46, keeping Tuesday's 3.9% gain as investors rotated into defensive dividend payers during the market's wild intraday swing. The drugmaker's calm stood out while the Nasdaq plunged 4.6% before recovering and the VIX spiked to 28.29. With markets closed for Thanksgiving, Pfizer's dividend yield keeps it on the safe-haven list heading into Friday's half session.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab bounced 2.3% Wednesday to $47.02, riding the market's late-day recovery after Tuesday's 7.4% slide. The space stock is one of the tape's most volatile names, swinging hard with risk appetite as the Nasdaq fell 4.6% intraday before clawing most of it back. No company news drove the move — pure sentiment — so Friday's thin half session could bring another sharp swing in either direction.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital gained 2.9% Wednesday to $8.92, extending a strong week as the mortgage REIT's dividend yield pulled in buyers during the market's flight to income. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.85% as stocks recovered from their intraday lows, a friendly backdrop for mortgage REITs. With a December Fed hike now priced near 95%, the rate path matters more than ever for Rithm's book value and payout.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: The leveraged S&P 500 fund rose 1.3% Wednesday to $127.44, tracking the market's late recovery with its usual amplified swing. The S&P fell 3.2% intraday before closing down just 0.25%, so the fund's gain reflects the furious afternoon buying rather than a calm day. Futures point higher into Friday, but leveraged funds cut both ways — a thin half session could magnify any move.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist added 0.9% Wednesday to $47.89, holding firm as the Dow climbed above 50,000 for the first time and banks caught a bid in the late recovery. Financials benefited as the 10-year yield held near 4.85% and the market priced a December hike as near-certain. With markets closed for Thanksgiving, Truist's next test is Friday's half session and whether the Dow can hold its round-number milestone.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony firmed 1.4% Wednesday to $2.21, steadying after Tuesday's 8.8% slide as small miners sold off. China's export curbs and U.S. critical-mineral policy remain the long-term bull case, but the stock still trades on risk appetite day to day. The Nasdaq's 4.6% intraday plunge and recovery set the tone; with futures higher into Friday, the antimony miner could keep steadying if sentiment holds.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy climbed 2.2% Wednesday to $5.69, recovering part of Tuesday's 4.6% slide in the market's late rebound. Nuclear expansion and U.S. uranium buying remain the structural story, but the stock is tied to risk appetite while the Fed's rate path dominates the tape. With oil jumping on Gulf tensions and futures pointing higher, the setup favors a steadier Friday session.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: VI5TC is estimated at $147.64, down 0.3% on the S&P 500's Wednesday slide, using the S&P-anchored estimator recalibrated from Dave's account value. The S&P fell as much as 3.2% intraday before closing down just 0.25%, so the estimate reflects the close, not the panic low. With U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving and futures pointing higher, the next estimate comes after Friday's half session.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero slipped 0.5% Wednesday to $323.00 even as the Dow hit 50,000, with oil seesawing and refiners giving back gains. Brent settled at $96.57 after Houthi strikes on Saudi ports and a refinery, then held firm as Iranian mines hit tankers in the strait Thursday. Higher crude lifts product prices but squeezes margins, so Valero's direction hinges on how far the supply scare runs.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: The Target Retirement 2035 fund's NAV nudged up to $28.45 as of Nov 25, a small gain as stocks recovered from intraday lows in the late session. The balanced fund's bond sleeve cushioned the Nasdaq's 4.6% intraday plunge, while its equity holdings joined the afternoon rebound. With markets closed for Thanksgiving, the next NAV prints after Friday's half session on a thin, holiday-shortened tape.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: SWVXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Schwab's 7-day SEC yield at 3.79% as published Nov 25, unchanged from the prior reading. The sweep fund keeps doing its quiet job while the market whipsaws — the VIX spiked to 28.29 Wednesday and the Nasdaq fell 4.6% intraday before recovering. Per the standing plan, balances above $1,000 get swept into CDs, so the position should keep shrinking toward zero over time.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: VUSXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Vanguard's 7-day SEC yield at 4.01% as published Nov 25, unchanged from the prior reading. The Treasury money fund remains the top-yielding cash parking spot on the board, comfortably ahead of Schwab's SWVXX at 3.79%. With markets closed for Thanksgiving and a December hike priced near 95%, money-fund yields should stay firm into Friday's half session and beyond.

weekInBrief.headline: Thanksgiving dinner costs $58.63, up 6% — first rise since 2022
weekInBrief.body: The American Farm Bureau's annual survey puts a classic Thanksgiving dinner for 10 at $58.63, or $5.86 a person — up 6% from 2025 and the first increase since 2022, though still below the $64.05 record. A 16-pound turkey at $23.68, up 10%, drove the rise, with milk, cranberries and dinner rolls also dearer; pie crusts and some produce got cheaper.

weekInBrief.headline: Eight shipping groups demand action to protect freedom of navigation
weekInBrief.body: Eight major shipping associations issued a joint open letter Thursday to EU foreign ministers calling for concrete measures to safeguard freedom of navigation and protect seafarers, backing the EU's Oct. 12 pledge on the law of the sea. Signatories include ECSA, BIMCO, CLIA, ICS, INTERCARGO, INTERFERRY, INTERTANKO and the World Shipping Council.

weekInBrief.headline: Black Friday: 182.7 million shoppers expected, and necessities join the gifts
weekInBrief.body: The National Retail Federation expects 182.7 million Americans to shop over the Thanksgiving weekend, with 126 million on Black Friday itself, and Adobe forecasts $12.9 billion in online Black Friday sales, up 9.2%. Shoppers are also using the deals to stock up on everyday goods — clothing basics, hygiene, baby and pet supplies are all surging versus September.

weekInBrief.headline: Salmonella found in 43% of Butterball ground turkey samples, no recall
weekInBrief.body: Federal inspection data analyzed by SourceMaterial and published with the Guardian on Nov. 25 found salmonella in just under 43% of ground or chopped turkey sampled over the past year at four Butterball plants, against the USDA's 13.5% standard; the Mount Olive, N.C. plant ran 36%. No recall followed and no illnesses were reported, and whole birds and cooked products tested clean.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Thursday that two tankers — one a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude — exploded and caught fire after hitting sea mines north of Oman's Khasab port, and that an LNG carrier suffered the same fate on an unauthorized route through the strait; the claims are unconfirmed, and UKMTO separately reported an explosion from an unidentified projectile near a tanker about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai. The incidents follow Wednesday's mine strikes and come as Gulf oil flows were recovering toward pre-war levels, keeping crude prices elevated on thin Thanksgiving trading. No Iranian oil is getting past the blockade: Kpler still puts Kharg loadings at zero and Iranian oil on water below 50 million barrels, with just 4.5 million outside the zone, while CENTCOM says Gulf partners shipped a record 108 million barrels of crude through the strait under U.S. protection last week, the largest weekly volume yet.

space.headline: Caltech's BrainBots carry chemo across the blood-brain barrier
space.body: Caltech researchers report in Science Robotics that light-activated nanorobots called BrainBots — tiny 250-nanometer capsules — delivered about five times more medication into mouse brains than the same bots without activation, ferrying the chemotherapy drug doxorubicin across the blood-brain barrier without disrupting it. In glioblastoma mouse models the bots slowed tumor growth and prolonged survival; human trials are still ahead.

space.headline: Deep-sea mussels seal shell damage with vaterite in 30 hours
space.body: In a cold-seep experiment reported in PNAS, deep-sea mussels (Gigantidas haimaensis) sealed acid-dissolved damage in their shells within 30 hours by secreting vaterite, a rare and unstable carbonate mineral, recrystallized from amorphous calcium carbonate. The rapid repair shows how these animals cope with corrosive deep water — and what acidifying oceans could cost them.

space.headline: Genetic analysis restores 12 coral species on the Great Barrier Reef
space.body: A James Cook University team combining genomic sequencing with historical museum specimens has restored species status to 12 Acropora corals long dismissed as variants of other species, and recognized four more previously unresolved ones, in a study published in Invertebrate Systematics. The Great Barrier Reef holds more coral diversity than realized — a finding that matters for judging extinction risk and reef health.

space.headline: ESCAPADE twins snap farewell photos of Earth on their way to Mars
space.body: NASA's twin ESCAPADE spacecraft photographed Earth in visible and infrared light on Nov. 9, about three hours after the second probe's powered Earth flyby, from 38,500 miles away with the Western Hemisphere in view and a solar panel cutting across the frame. The two craft, the first Martian probes to use a powered Earth flyby, are now on a roughly 10-month cruise to Mars, arriving in September 2027.

apod.title: Webb Sees Turbulent Star Nursery
apod.credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, E. Sabbi, M. Zamani (ESA/Webb) — NASA Image of the Day, Oct. 28, 2026
apod.explanation: A turbulent cauldron of star formation fills this Webb view of N159, a region of dense gas clumps 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud, one of the Milky Way's satellite galaxies. Wispy blue gas forms delicate layers around thicker orange clouds with dark ridges, and glowing bubbles hold dense, bright clusters of young stars. The region's lower metallicity gives astronomers a window on conditions in the early universe and how stars formed there.
